name: Rollins, Inc.

corporate_actions.event: Q3 2026: revenue +6.2%, organic +4.4% (residential +2.3%), operating margin -140bp to 20.5%; missed consensus; 2026 organic outlook reportedly cut to 4-6% (secondary source, unverified against release)
Secondary offering by Rollins family-affiliated holder with concurrent company repurchase (recall, not re-verified)

geography.fx_notes: Orkin and brand portfolio predominantly US with Canada, Australia, UK and franchise operations; INFERENCE: US ~90% of revenue (not extracted). China 0 = no operations.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.value: 20.5% (-140bp y/y); insurance & claims 3.4% of revenue vs 1.8%

kpis.name: Residential lead generation
kpis.value: Management cites shift of customer discovery to AI-driven search; marketing reallocated

kpis.name: Customer retention / technician productivity
kpis.value: not disclosed numerically in sources retrieved

company_fcf.definition: Company FCF = operating cash flow less capex

lease.source_id: US GAAP filer (operating leases in EBITDA); not extracted

acquisitions.notes: Incl. Saela (residential door-to-door, 2025, recall); capex $28m; dividends $328m

management.senior_turnover_5y: Orderly: Gary Rollins handed CEO role to internal successor 2022/23 (recall)
management.guidance_record: Strong 2021-2024; 2025-26 misses (Q4-25 and Q3-26 below expectations; 2026 organic target cut from 7-8%)

ownership.controlling_holders: Rollins family entities hold a large minority (recall ~30-40% historically; reduced after 2024 sale; not re-verified)
ownership.board_independence: Historically 'controlled company' characteristics; independence below peers (recall, L)
ownership.related_party: Family-related arrangements historically (aircraft/real estate) small; not reviewed this run

guidance.value: Reportedly 4-6% (from prior ~7-8% target); incremental margin slightly positive to 10% (secondary source)

evidence: Residential acquisition slowed to +2.3% in Q3-26 [S1]
A.rationale: Highly recurring, but residential new-customer flow is more discretionary/marketing-dependent.

B.rationale: Brand plus density with demonstrable margin advantage; but low switching costs in residential.

evidence: Margin above Rentokil NA despite smaller scale
C.rationale: Local density economics evident; not a 5 because AI-search disruption shows acquisition-funnel vulnerability.

evidence: Fragmented US market, bolt-on M&A adds ~3-4pts/yr [S2]
D.rationale: Long runway via tuck-ins and commercial growth.

evidence: Q4-25 and Q3-26 misses; 2026 organic target cut [S1][S2]
F.rationale: Strong long-term record now mixed with recent misses.

G.rationale: Disciplined bolt-on M&A at sensible leverage.

H.rationale: Aligned but with weaker independence; noted neutrally.

evidence: But AI search is disrupting residential lead generation [S1]
I1.rationale: Service immune; customer-acquisition channel exposed to AI intermediaries.

evidence: Low cyclicality; insurance/claims cost inflation hit Q3 margin [S1]
J.rationale: Resilient demand; some cost volatility (claims, vehicles, labour).

K.rationale: Cash > profit; claims provisioning worth monitoring.

ai.notes: No AI capex dependence. Contrary evidence: AI-driven search is changing how residential customers find providers (Q3-26 call).

sector_specific.route_density_note: Highest margin in pest peer group (provider EBIT ~18%)

gates.notes: Provider ND/EBITDA 1.2x. FCF $650m vs NI ~$520m. No transaction pending. US residential consumer-linked but not UK consumer/travel.

bull_points: Highest-margin scaled pest operator with 7-8% organic history and bolt-on runway.
Recurring commercial and termite renewal base with low cyclicality.
Minimal AI disruption to the service itself.
bear_points: Organic growth decelerated from 7-8% to 4.4% in Q3-26 with residential at 2.3%; AI search changing lead acquisition may raise marketing cost structurally.
Margins fell 140bp as insurance/claims costs doubled as % of revenue.
Premium valuation (provider EV/EBITDA ~18x TTM) with US-only exposure.
thesis_breakers: Operating margin below 19% for two consecutive years.
Termite/insurance claim costs above 3% of revenue on a full-year basis.
